decisions.reason: The client replaces the shared length-and-terminal study with a height-only progression, keeps the Option B terminal fixed, and postpones accent propagation until a percentage is selected.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hi Abdulbari,

Somewhere my intended message got lost in translation. I know it’s hard to read my mind when I use more abstract terms, and I think I was trying to ask you to change too many things at once, which is why we have taken a couple of steps in the wrong direction.

I’m attaching this image for reference because it was the closest rendering to what I wanted to refine. Instead of changing the length and exploring the terminations at the same time, we’re going to focus strictly on height.

Could you please show the following as a calibrated progression in both the Hero V and the second V? The second V should remain proportionally scaled to its own size, so each increase should be calculated relative to the total height of that individual V.

Original Option B as the control
Original Option B with the right endpoint approximately 1% higher
The same treatment at approximately 2% higher
The same treatment at approximately 3% higher

Please keep the existing slope, terminal shape, taper, and all other geometry exactly as shown in the original Option B. Only the height of the right endpoint should change. Once the correct percentage is established, the É accent should follow that same proportional relationship.

I know this is an exceptionally small distinction, but I believe the relationship between the left and right endpoints will become one of the defining details shared across the Hero V, second V, and É accent. I want it to be almost imperceptible, but still enough to distinguish it from a more average V.

Thank you for helping me isolate it with this level of precision.

value_updates.experimental_control: Original Option B with its slope, terminal shape, taper, and all other geometry unchanged while only the right-endpoint height varies
value_updates.consistency_rule: Apply the calibrated progression to the Hero V and second V relative to each glyph's own height; after the percentage is established, the É accent follows the same proportional relationship

decisions.reason: The client explicitly replaces the second V's prior reach/length treatment with a proportional endpoint-height study while locking its other geometry.

The source defines a geometry study relative to the second V's own height but does not change its established hierarchy relative to the Hero V, É accent, E, or L.
Requiring the accent to follow the selected proportional relationship does not revoke or modify the existing exact peak-alignment rule.
The source concerns glyph endpoint height and explicitly keeps other design variables fixed; it makes no material or color decision.
The height-only study does not change the selected Balanced Flow kerning or cohesive-reading requirement.
Changing the right endpoints of the V glyphs does not change the E/L cap-height rule based on the second V's left arm.
The source changes only right-endpoint height and does not alter the common baseline or either V's bottom point.
The design-study instructions do not modify the independent requirement to provide rationale with review rounds.
